name: BuddyPress Default Cover Photo
author: SeventhQueen

sections.description:
The plugin adds DEFAULT Profile and Group cover settings in WP Admin – Settings – BuddyPress – Options.

You also have the option to replace default BuddyPress cover photo and use this plugin for the cover functionality.

Check out this demo to see it in action:
http://seventhqueen.com/themes/kleo/members/kleoadmin/
sections.installation:
To Install:

  1. Download the plugin file
  2. Unzip the file into a folder on your hard drive
  3. Upload the /buddypress-cover-photo/ folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ folder on your site
  4. Single-site BuddyPress go to Plugins menu and activate there.
  5. For Multisite visit Network Admin -> Plugins and Network Activate it there.
sections.faq:
BuddyPress has built-in cover images. Do I still need this plugin?

BuddyPress has its own profile and group cover images since version 2.4. They are turned on in WP admin – Settings – BuddyPress – Options with “Allow registered members to upload cover images” and “Allow customizable cover images for groups”.

The plugin works in one of two modes:

  • Default (recommended): BuddyPress cover images are used. The plugin only adds the default profile and group covers set in Settings – BuddyPress – Options, and keeps showing the covers uploaded earlier with the plugin as each member’s or group’s default, until a new cover is uploaded with the BuddyPress “Change Cover Image” screen. Deleting a cover in BuddyPress also deletes the old plugin cover.
  • Replace: when “Replace BP 2.4 functionality” is checked, the plugin cover uploader is used and the BuddyPress cover images are turned off, so covers are never displayed twice. Covers uploaded with BuddyPress stay on disk and come back when the option is unchecked.

The settings section shows which mode is active. If your theme does not support BuddyPress cover images, the default mode cannot display any cover; check “Replace BP 2.4 functionality” to use the plugin covers.

How do I move from the plugin covers to the BuddyPress cover images?

  1. In WP admin – Settings – BuddyPress – Options, uncheck “Replace BP 2.4 functionality” and make sure the BuddyPress cover image options are checked.
  2. Existing plugin covers keep showing as each member’s and group’s default cover, so nothing disappears.
  3. Members and group admins upload a new cover with “Change Cover Image” when they want to. There is no automatic file migration; the old plugin files stay in the uploads folder until the cover is deleted or replaced.

Which data does the plugin store?

  • Options: bpcp-enabled (replace mode), bpcp-profile-default, bpcp-group-default (default cover URLs).
  • User meta: profile_cover (image URL), profile_cover_file_path (file path), profile_cover_pos (position: center, top or bottom).
  • Group meta: bpcp_group_cover, bpcp_group_cover_file_path, bpcp_group_cover_pos.

What other configurations do I need

No. This plugin needs no configuration.

How do I set up default cover images

From WP admin – Settings – BuddyPress – Options you can set default images for profile and groups.
sections.changelog:
1.6.1 (2026-11-13)

  • Maintenance release, no new features
  • Compatibility with WordPress 7.1, BuddyPress 14 (BP Nouveau and BP Legacy) and PHP 7.4 to 8.5
  • Fixed: with “Replace BP 2.4 functionality” checked, BuddyPress 6.0+ also displayed its own profile cover, so profiles showed two covers. The plugin now turns the BuddyPress members cover images off with the current filter
  • Fixed: PHP deprecation notices from the BuddyPress filters renamed in 6.0 and the URL functions deprecated in 12.0
  • Fixed: deleting a group cover from the group admin screen did not work
  • Fixed: upload size limit when memory_limit is -1
  • Security: capability checks on the cover delete requests, so members can only delete their own covers (and group admins their group covers)
  • Security: uploads are limited to real JPG, GIF and PNG images; old files are only deleted from the uploads folder
  • Security: escaped all output and sanitized the settings and form input
  • Added a notice in Settings – BuddyPress – Options that explains whether the BuddyPress or the plugin cover images are in use
  • Readme: documented the BuddyPress built-in cover images, how to move to them and the stored meta keys
